note: Peak RSS of the QUERY path: the SQLite index resident, plus for `get` one document decoded. Compare results-rss-core.json, which measures .lxz encode and decode and knows nothing about the index. Sizes are exact; RSS is indicative on this container but the shape (flat search, linear-in-document get) is the point.
how_measured: os.fork + os.execve of `lexora db search` / `lexora db get`, reading ru_maxrss from os.wait4. The catalog is built in a CHILD process: a forked child inherits the parent's footprint, and an earlier version of this probe reported its own fixture's RSS as the CLI's.

findings.search_is_flat_in_archive_size: 27.2 -> 27.9 MiB while the index grew 4x; the interpreter alone is ~16 MiB
findings.get_tracks_the_decoded_document: 30.2 -> 40.8 MiB as documents went 1 MiB -> 4 MiB, i.e. ~3x the document size
findings.index_pct: 12.8% of text at 4 MiB, 5.4% at 16 MiB — the fixed cost dominates small catalogs, matching the ~7% ADR-0016 measured on real prose
findings.against_a_4GiB_target: a 16 MiB catalog peaks under 41 MiB; nothing here threatens the 4 GiB budget

not_measured: a catalog large enough to test the ADR-0016 claim that the index scales at ~7% of text — that needs tens of GiB of input, which is what the 4 GiB machine run is for. --cap-mib makes that run a pass/fail gate.
